newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-German shares hit record, holiday slows forex.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-German shares hit record, holiday slows forex.

text.p: German stocks hit record levels on Monday after Friday's strong Wall Street performance and the dollar was steady, but activity on European markets was muted with London and Tokyo closed for holidays.
Wall Street's storming close last week, following an agreement to balance the U.S. budget, gave German shares the biggest boost although the Paris bourse also rose after a weak start.
The DAX index burst through its previous peak of 3,474.98 points at the opening and by mid morning it was up 64.18 points (1.85 percent) at 3,524.55.
The Dow Jones industrial average on Friday soared 94.72 points, or 1.36 percent, to close at 7,071.20 -- close to its record high.
U.S. bonds also rose sharply after President Bill Clinton announced he had reached a landmark agreement with Republican leaders in Congress on a plan to balance the federal budget by 2002.
Automobile stocks led the way in Germany due to the steady dollar but trading volumes were expected to be limited by the absence of London-based investors.
Shares in computer software maker SAP SAPG._P.f slipped 1.90 marks to 319.50 after prosecutors said they were investigating a potentially serious case of insider trading in the stock.
French shares turned higher after a weak start but again volume was low due to the London holiday.
The market drew support from a BVA opinion poll showing that the ruling centre-right coalition and other conservative parties could win 294 seats in the parliamentary elections in late May and June.
This showed an increase for the right following weekend polls showing the Socialist party reducing the conservatives' lead. The blue-chip CAC-40 index gained 9.18 points or 0.35 percent to 2,664.49.
Prime Minister Alain Juppe said on Monday that the election race was getting closer: "I have always thought the vote would be close." he said.
Political risk was restricting trading volumes, traders said. But one trader said. "Everybody more or less takes the view the conservatives will get in, even with a reduced majority."
Italian shares opened slightly higher but Mediobanca, HPI and Marzotto, whose plan to plan to create a super textiles group collapsed at the weekend, all took a heavy drubbing.
The foreign exchange markets were particularly subdued by the British and Japanese holidays.
The dollar was steady against the yen and mark in early Europe, although off overnight highs. "The dollar has been rangebound," said a trader at a Swedish bank.

By mid morning the dollar was trading at 1.7270 marks against 1.7273 in late Europe on Friday, although off overnight highs just above 1.73 marks. Against the yen, it was trading at 126.70 against 126.63 on Friday.

Overall, the dollar was in good shape after the release of Friday's U.S. employment data, which eased fears of inflation even though unemployment was at its lowest level in 23 years, and news of the balanced budget agreement.
Sterling slipped against the mark, with markets attentive as the new Labour government under Prime Minister Tony Blair begin first full week of power.
Markets were focused on Wednesday's monetary meeting between new Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown and Bank of England Governor Eddie George.
Speculation is growing that Brown will sanction the interest rate rise the central bank has long urged.
Sterling was quoted at 2.7973 marks against 2.8052 in late European trading on Friday.
STOCKS AT 0845 GMT
The Paris CAC-40 index was up 9.18 points at 2,664.49.
Frankfurt's DAX index was up 64.18 points (1.85 percent) at 3,524.55.
The London market was closed for a public holiday. On Friday the FTSE 100 closed up 17.2 points at 4,462.2.
CURRENCIES AT 0845 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.7270 marks compared with 1.7273 marks late in Europe on Friday. It was at 126.70 yen after 126.63 yen late on Friday.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was at $340.50 an ounce after closing on Friday at $340.05 an ounce in London.
